s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: to consume food, usually solids, but also liquids{N:001}
s.g: to eat; to drink; to consume food; to use food
s.c: As noted in the contexts of ⟦Matthew 12:1|Matthew 12:1⟧ and ⟦1 Corinthians 9:7|1 Corinthians 9:7⟧, ἐσθίω is generic in the sense that it includes the consumption of both solid foods and liquids, but ἐσθίω is not employed in referring to the drinking of alcoholic beverages (see μεθύω to drink freely of wine or beer, LN 23.37).|In some languages an important distinction is made in terms for ‘eating’ depending upon whether the eating is done by an adult or by a very small child, who in most instances must be helped to eat. Other distinctions in terminology for eating may involve the quantities of food (whether small or extensive), the rapidity with which one eats (gulping or mincing), the state of what is eaten (raw, fresh, cooked) or the type of food, for example, meat, cereal, fruit, or leafy vegetable.

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Destroy
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἐσθίω<SDBG:ἐσθίω:000000>}[a] ‘to eat,’ {D:23.1}) to destroy, with the implication of doing away with all traces of an object

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Earn, Gain, Do Business

s.g: to earn a living; to earn a livelihood

s.dp: Animal Husbandry, Fishing
s.d: to put something over or around the mouths of animals so as to prevent them from eating
s.g: to muzzle; to keep from eating
s.c: In some languages it may be necessary to employ some type of descriptive equivalent of ‘to muzzle,’ for example, ‘do not tie the mouth of the ox so that it cannot eat’ or ‘do not cover the mouth of the ox so that it cannot eat.’

s.g: to have nothing to say; to say nothing

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Humility
s.d: pertaining to having the attitude of humility

s.dp: Plants › Plants That Are Not Trees
s.d: small aromatic bush with a shrub-like base and stems which are stiff, many-branched, hairy, and strong, 50-80 cm tall; Origanum syriacum or Majorana syriaca; used by the Jews in the ritual purification process as a sprinkling brush
s.c: The hyssop bush may reach a height of one meter (three feet) and has a number of woody stems.|In some translations a term for ‘hyssop’ is borrowed with a classifier such as ‘plant,’ for example, ‘a branch of a plant called hyssop.’|In ⟦John 19:29|John 19:29⟧ some translators have simply used ‘a twig’ or ‘a branch,’ but this may not be adequate, since some persons see a good deal of symbolism in the use of the term ‘hyssop’ because of its relationship to ritual uses in the OT.|According to an old conjecture, the text of ⟦John 19:29|John 19:29⟧ could have contained the term ὑσσός ‘javelin’ (LN 6.35) rather than ὕσσωπος ‘hyssop’ (this reading is actually found in one eleventh century minuscule manuscript), and this has been followed by the NEB translation (“they soaked a sponge with the wine, fixed it on a javelin …”), but this form of the text has very little support and is not recommended.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Need, Lack
s.d: to be lacking in what is essential or needed{N:001}
s.g: to lack; to be in need of; to be in want

s.g: to lack benefits; to lack an advantage

s.dp: Status › Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
s.d: to be in a state of low status

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to fail in some measure to attain some state or condition
s.g: to fail to attain; to not attain; to be behind in

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Need, Lack

s.g: what is lacking; what is needed
s.c: In a number of languages the expression of ‘lack’ may be indicated as ‘not to have enough’ or ‘not to possess what one needs’ or ‘not to have what one should have.’

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: absence as an element of lack or deficiency

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Need, Lack
s.d: to be lacking in what is essential or needed{N:001}
s.g: to lack; to be in need of; to be in want

s.dp: Sequence
s.d: pertaining to being final in a series, but probably not as emphatic as {L:ἔσχατος<SDBG:ἔσχατος:000000>}[a] ‘last,’ {D:61.13}

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After

s.dp: Activities Involving Cloth
s.d: (derivative of {L:ὑφαίνω<SDBG:ὑφαίνω:000000>} ‘to weave,’ {D:48.3}) pertaining to being woven
s.c: In a number of languages it may be best to translate the last part of ⟦John 19:23|John 19:23⟧ as simply ‘it was only one piece of cloth’ or ‘it was not made by sewing pieces of cloth together.’

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › High, Low, Deep
s.d: pertaining to being high

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Regions Above the Earth
s.d: a location above the earth and associated with supernatural events or beings
s.g: high; world above; sky; heaven; on high
s.c: In contexts in which these expressions refer clearly to ‘heaven’ or ‘the sky,’ it is better to use terms meaning ‘heaven’ or ‘sky’ rather than terms meaning ‘height’ or ‘that which is high.’

s.dp: Value › Valuable, Lacking in Value
s.d: pertaining to being regarded as of particular value, implying evident comparison with other items
s.c: For another interpretation of ὑψηλός in ⟦Luke 16:15|Luke 16:15⟧, see LN 88.208.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Arrogance, Haughtiness, Pride
s.d: pertaining to being arrogant or proud
s.c: The phrase τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὑψηλόν may be rendered in some languages as ‘that which people think is great’ or ‘that which people think is very good indeed.’ For another interpretation of ὑψηλός in ⟦Luke 16:15|Luke 16:15⟧, see LN 65.9.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Arrogance, Haughtiness, Pride
s.d: to have an arrogant, haughty attitude
s.g: to be haughty; to be arrogant

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Above, Below
s.d: (comparative of {L:ὑψηλός<SDBG:ὑψηλός:000000>}[a] ‘high,’ {D:81.6}) a position above another, on the basis of being higher

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Arrogance, Haughtiness, Pride
s.d: to have an arrogant, haughty attitude
s.g: to be haughty; to be arrogant
s.c: The meaning of ‘to be haughty’ may be expressed in a number of languages as ‘to regard oneself as better than anyone else.’

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Regions Above the Earth
s.d: a location above the earth and associated with supernatural events or beings
s.g: high; world above; sky; heaven; on high
s.c: The parallelism in the phrases peace in heaven and glory in the world above indicates quite clearly the equivalence in reference, though not in meaning, between οὐρανός (LN 1.11) and ὕψιστος.|In ⟦Matthew 21:9|Matthew 21:9⟧ the phrase ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις, literally ‘hosanna in the highest,’ has been interpreted as a plea for salvation or deliverance from God who is in heaven. However, it seems preferable to understand ὡσαννά as simply being a shout of exclamation or praise and therefore to interpret the phrase ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις as meaning ‘praise to God.’ In ⟦Luke 19:38|Luke 19:38⟧ a parallel expression, καὶ δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις, literally ‘and glory in the highest,’ is usually understood as an acclamation of glory to God and therefore may be so rendered. See LN 33.357.|In contexts in which these expressions refer clearly to ‘heaven’ or ‘the sky,’ it is better to use terms meaning ‘heaven’ or ‘sky’ rather than terms meaning ‘height’ or ‘that which is high.’

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (a title for God, literally: highest) one who is supreme, primarily a reference to status
s.g: the Most High; the Highest; the Supreme One
s.c: In some languages the concept of height is entirely unrelated to the idea of importance, and therefore it may be necessary to translate ‘the Most High’ as ‘the Most Important’ or even ‘the Greatest.’

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › High, Low, Deep
s.d: the measurement of height
s.c: In ⟦Ephesians 3:18|Ephesians 3:18⟧ the four different dimensions of space are used figuratively in the sense of ‘that which is all-encompassing.’

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Regions Above the Earth
s.d: a location above the earth and associated with supernatural events or beings
s.g: high; world above; sky; heaven; on high
s.c: In ⟦Luke 24:49|Luke 24:49⟧ ὕψος refers to heaven as a type of substitute reference for God, and in many languages it is advisable to translate ‘until the power from God comes down on you.’ In ⟦Ephesians 4:8|Ephesians 4:8⟧ the phrase ἀναβὰς εἰς ὕψος may be rendered literally as ‘when he went up to the heights,’ but it is preferable in a number of languages to translate ‘when he went up to heaven,’ for a literal rendering of ‘heights’ might imply only a high building or a mountain.|In contexts in which these expressions refer clearly to ‘heaven’ or ‘the sky,’ it is better to use terms meaning ‘heaven’ or ‘sky’ rather than terms meaning ‘height’ or ‘that which is high.’

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a position of high status

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Light
s.d: (an idiom, literally: dawning from on high) the bright dawn of salvation (or possibly to be understood as a title for the Messiah)
s.c: The expression ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους occurs in a highly poetic liturgical passage in Luke 1, and many translators have preferred to retain the more or less literal rendering. Others, however, have interpreted this as the dawning of salvation and have therefore translated ἐπισκέψεται ἡμᾶς ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους as ‘salvation will dawn upon us from heaven’ or ‘from heaven salvation will come to us as the dawn does.’ If one wishes to employ ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους as simply a title for the Messiah, one can translate ‘the Messiah will come to us,’ but it is normally better to preserve the figurative expression and relate it to the coming of the Messiah as ‘the Messiah will come to us even as the dawn does from on high.’ One may also treat the problem of interpretation in a footnote.

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › High, Low, Deep
s.d: to cause something to become high
s.g: to raise up; to lift up

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: to cause someone to have high status
s.g: to give high position to; to exalt

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Regions Above the Earth
s.d: a location above the earth and associated with supernatural events or beings
s.g: high; world above; sky; heaven; on high
s.c: There are differences of scholarly opinion as to whether ὕψωμα in ⟦Romans 8:39|Romans 8:39⟧ is to be understood as a dimension of space (and as such, related to certain Pythagorean or NeoPlatonic concepts of elemental forces) or as the world above (as the location of alien demonic forces). For another interpretation of ὕψωμα in ⟦Romans 8:39|Romans 8:39⟧, see LN 12.46.|In contexts in which these expressions refer clearly to ‘heaven’ or ‘the sky,’ it is better to use terms meaning ‘heaven’ or ‘sky’ rather than terms meaning ‘height’ or ‘that which is high.’

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Powers
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ὕψωμα[a] ‘world above,’ {D:1.13}) supernatural powers in the region above the earth
s.c: For another interpretation of ὕψωμα in ⟦Romans 8:39|Romans 8:39⟧, see LN 1.13.|It is possible that ὕψωμα in ⟦Romans 8:39|Romans 8:39⟧ should be interpreted merely as a reference to the distance which a person might be separated from God.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Arrogance, Haughtiness, Pride
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ὕψωμα ‘height,’ not occurring in the NT) an exaggerated evaluation of what one is or of what one has done

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: (derivative of the stem φαγ- ‘to eat,’ the aorist of {L:ἐσθίω<SDBG:ἐσθίω:000000>}[a], {D:23.1}) a person who habitually eats excessively
s.c: A glutton is often spoken of idiomatically, for example, ‘a large belly’ or ‘a person who is only a stomach’ or ‘a professional eater.’

s.dp: Artifacts › Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
s.d: any type of outer garment{N:001}
s.c: The choice of an equivalent for these terms relating to ‘outer garments’ will depend largely upon the specific context and the usage in each receptor language. The most common equivalent is a term meaning ‘coat.’

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Light
s.d: to shine or to produce light, as in the case of heavenly bodies, lightning, candles, torches, etc.
s.g: to shine; to give light; to bring light
s.c: Terms for ‘shining, giving light’ often differ depending upon the type of source. There may be, for example, a contrast between the shining of a heavenly body in contrast with some source on earth. There may also be a difference between a continuous shining such as of the sun and the moon and a brief flash, as in the case of lightning or sparks from a fire.

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: to become visible to someone
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘appeared to’ would simply be ‘came to’ or ‘arrived at.’ In other languages the equivalent is ‘… he saw in a dream.’

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: to cause something to be fully known by revealing clearly and in some detail{N:001}
s.g: to make known; to make plain; to reveal; to bring to the light; to disclose; revelation

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: to make known only the superficial and not the real character of something
s.g: to appear to be (something); to give an impression of
s.c: In order to do justice to φαίνομαι in ⟦Matthew 23:28|Matthew 23:28⟧, it may be necessary in some languages to translate as follows: ‘on the outside you appear to people to be good, but you really are not’ or ‘… you only appear to people to be good’ or ‘… you make people think you are good, but you are not.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: pertaining to being widely and well known
s.c: In some languages it may be necessary in translating ⟦Mark 6:14|Mark 6:14⟧ to reverse certain roles, for example, ‘people everywhere came to know about Jesus.’

s.dp: Know › Able To Be Known
s.d: pertaining to being clearly and easily able to be known
s.g: clearly known; easily known; evident; plain; clear
s.c: For some of the problems involved in the rendering of ⟦Romans 1:19|Romans 1:19⟧, see the discussion under γνωστός (LN 28.57).

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: (derivative of the stem φαν- ‘to appear,’ {D:24.18}, {D:24.19}) pertaining to that which appears clear or evident
s.c: In view of the contrast which exists in ⟦Romans 2:28|Romans 2:28⟧ between ἐν τῷ φανερῷ and ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ, it is, of course, possible to translate ἐν τῷ φανερῷ as ‘that which is external’ and ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ as ‘that which is internal,’ but it would seem better to preserve the contrast as ‘that which can be seen’ and ‘that which cannot be seen.’ See LN 24.29.

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: to cause to become visible
s.g: to make appear; to make visible; to cause to be seen
s.c: In a number of languages the meaning of ‘appeared to’ must be expressed as two closely related events, so that in ⟦John 21:1|John 21:1⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘Jesus came and was seen once more by his disciples’ or ‘Jesus came and once more his disciples saw him.’

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: to cause something to be fully known by revealing clearly and in some detail{N:001}
s.g: to make known; to make plain; to reveal; to bring to the light; to disclose; revelation

s.dp: Know › Able To Be Known
s.d: pertaining to the manner by which something can easily be known by the public, with the implication that the related events take place in the open
s.c: The expression ‘he did not go openly’ (⟦John 7:10|John 7:10⟧) may often be rendered as ‘he did not go about where people could see him’ or ‘people did not see where he was.’

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: (derivative of the stem φαν- ‘to appear,’ {D:24.18}, {D:24.19}) pertaining to that which appears clear or evident

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: to cause something to be fully known by revealing clearly and in some detail{N:001}
s.g: to make known; to make plain; to reveal; to bring to the light; to disclose; revelation

s.dp: Artifacts › Lights and Light Holders
s.d: a small fire which was carried about for the sake of its light and which had some type of protection from wind and weather
s.c: Though φανός in earlier Greek meant a torch, by NT times it appears to have been used primarily to identify a type of lamp used outdoors.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of Anna the prophetess

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: to become visible, implying an extraordinary and startling appearance

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a pompous ceremony, implying a cheap display of high status

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: an apparition
s.c: Most languages have quite satisfactory terms for ‘ghosts’ or ‘apparitions,’ since the psychological phenomena associated with such appearances are apparently universal. In some languages the equivalent of ‘ghost’ is simply ‘shadow.’ In other instances it may be literally ‘breath.’ In some instances the meaning of ‘ghost’ is incorporated within a verb expression, for example, ‘they saw, as it were, through him.’|The NT contains a number of lexical items (LN 12.43-LN 12.47) referring to supernatural powers believed to be active as elemental spirits exercising control over man’s fate. Though these may have certain special features associated with them and though in extrabiblical literature they may represent various grades of supernatural power, there seems to be no way in which they can be clearly distinguished on the basis of their NT usage. Appropriate equivalent expressions in other languages are extremely difficult to find, primarily because other religious systems usually have completely different beliefs relative to supernatural powers. In many languages it is simply not possible to speak of such supernatural powers without in some way identifying them with various kinds of spirits.

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Depressions and Holes
s.c: φάραγξ, as ‘a narrow valley,’ differs from ‘a broad valley’ in the sense that one does not expect agriculture to be practiced at the bottom of a φάραγξ, while in the case of a broad valley, agriculture would be an assumed feature.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a title used as a proper name of the Egyptian king

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a member of an important religious and political Jewish party at the time of Jesus and the apostles. The Pharisees constituted a significantly larger group than the Sadducees (see {D:11.48}) and differed with them on certain doctrines and patterns of behavior. The Pharisees were strict and jealous adherents to the laws of the OT and to numerous additional traditions
s.c: Translators have generally found it both wise and necessary to simply transliterate in one form or another Σαδδουκαῖος (LN 11.48) and Φαρισαῖος, but some background information concerning these two parties is particularly important in a glossary; otherwise, certain passages of Scripture become extremely difficult to understand satisfactorily.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Magic
s.d: the use of magic, often involving drugs and the casting of spells upon people
s.g: to practice magic; to cast spells upon; to engage in sorcery; magic; sorcery
s.c: φαρμακεία and the variant φάρμακον (as in ⟦Revelation 9:21|Revelation 9:21⟧) differ from the preceding terms (LN 53.96-LN 53.99) in that the focus is upon the use of certain potions or drugs and the casting of spells.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Magic
s.d: the use of magic, often involving drugs and the casting of spells upon people
s.g: to practice magic; to cast spells upon; to engage in sorcery; magic; sorcery
s.c: φαρμακεία and the variant φάρμακον (as in ⟦Revelation 9:21|Revelation 9:21⟧) differ from the preceding terms (LN 53.96-LN 53.99) in that the focus is upon the use of certain potions or drugs and the casting of spells.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Magic
s.d: (derivative of {L:φαρμακεία<SDBG:φαρμακεία:000000>} ‘to practice magic, to engage in sorcery,’ {D:53.100}) one who uses magic and sorcery

s.dp: Communication › Inform, Announce
s.d: information concerning a person or an event

s.dp: Communication › Assert, Declare
s.d: to speak about something with certainty

s.dp: Artifacts › Containers
s.d: a box or crib where animals feed (or possibly even an open feeding place under the sky)
s.c: φάτνη occurs only in ⟦Luke 2:7|Luke 2:7⟧, and it may be important in some languages to distinguish clearly between various alternatives. The term ‘crib’ normally refers to the place where an animal stands when it feeds. The ‘manger’ is a relatively large box or rack containing hay, and a ‘feed box’ is a much smaller container, usually for grain. There is, of course, no way of knowing precisely where the baby Jesus was placed, but it would be very appropriate for the baby to have been placed in the feed box or in the manger. See also LN 7.64.

s.dp: Constructions › Miscellaneous Constructions
s.d: a stall where animals are fed
s.c: φάτνη may designate a part of a barn, or it may simply refer to a customary place where an animal is fed outside, often in a semi-enclosure (see LN 6.137).

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Bad, Evil, Harmful, Damaging
s.d: pertaining to being evil in the sense of moral baseness

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Light
s.d: light, in contrast with darkness ({L:σκότος<SDBG:σκότος:000000>}[a], {L:σκοτία<SDBG:σκοτία:000000>}[a], {D:14.53}), usually in relationship to some source of light such as the sun, moon, fire, lamp, etc.{N:001}
s.c: Terms for ‘light’ often differ on the basis of whether there is a specific source of light, for example, a fire, lamps, sun, moon, etc., or whether the light is simply generalized, in the sense of daylight apart from the actual shining of the sun (for example, as in the interior of a room). Some languages also make distinctions between terms for light depending on whether the light comes from a fire or lamp or from a heavenly body.|In a number of languages there is no noun for ‘light,’ but only verbs are employed, since the fact of light is spoken of as something which happens and is hence regarded as an event.

s.dp: Trouble, Hardship, Relief, Favorable Circumstances › Cause Trouble, Hardship
s.d: to cause someone not to be troubled
s.g: to spare; to prevent trouble happening to someone

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to keep oneself from doing something
s.g: to avoid; to refrain from; to keep oneself from

s.dp: Quantity › Abundance, Excess, Sparing
s.d: pertaining to what is done in a limited, sparing manner and of negligible quantity or extent
s.c: In ⟦2 Corinthians 9:6|2 Corinthians 9:6⟧ φειδομένως is obviously in contrast with the phrase ἐπ᾽ εὐλογίαις ‘abundantly’ (LN 59.56). It may, however, be necessary to indicate clearly the nature of that which is sown or reaped sparingly, for example, ‘the one who plants only a small amount of seed will have only a very small harvest.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Carry, Bear
s.d: to bear or carry something from one place to another
s.g: to carry; to bear; to take along

s.dp: Linear Movement › Lead, Bring, Take
s.d: to cause to move to a place, with a possible implication of assistance or firm control
s.g: to take; to carry; to bring

s.dp: Linear Movement › Drive Along, Carry Along
s.d: to cause an object to move by means of a force
s.g: to drive along; to carry along

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Guide, Lead
s.d: to so influence others as to cause them to follow a recommended course of action
s.g: to guide; to direct; to lead
s.c: In some languages it is difficult to distinguish readily between expressions for ‘leading’ and those which refer to ‘ruling’ or ‘governing,’ but it is important to try to distinguish clearly between these two different sets of interpersonal relations. In some languages, the concept of ‘leading’ can be expressed by ‘showing how to’ or ‘demonstrating how one ought to.’ In other languages it is possible to speak of ‘leading’ as simply ‘going ahead of,’ but too often such an expression may designate only ‘a scout’ who goes ahead to see whether things are safe, or it may refer only to a person who insists on his prerogative as the most distinguished person in a group.

s.dp: Spacial Orientations › Left, Right, Straight Ahead, Opposite
s.d: to be oriented in the direction of a movement
s.g: to lead to; to lead into

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to cause something adverse to happen to someone, usually in connection with accusations or condemnations
s.g: to bring against; to cause to happen to; to bring about

s.dp: Existence in Space › Put, Place
s.d: to put or place an object by moving it to a particular point

s.dp: Case › Experiencer
s.d: to experience an event or state which may be burdensome or difficult
s.g: to experience; to bear up under; to undergo

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to cause to continue by sustaining or maintaining a state
s.c: In some languages, however, the closest equivalent of this expression in ⟦Hebrews 1:3|Hebrews 1:3⟧ may be ‘causing everything to continue to be as it is by his powerful word.’|It is also possible to interpret φέρω in ⟦Hebrews 1:3|Hebrews 1:3⟧ as ‘to cause to continue to exist,’ in which case it may be classified after LN 13.89. However, the focus seems to be on the state of being.

s.dp: Real, Unreal
s.d: to present evidence that something has actually happened
s.g: to show something happened; to demonstrate something was real
s.c: In rendering φέρω in ⟦Hebrews 9:16|Hebrews 9:16⟧, it may be necessary to redistribute the semantic components even as in the case of the English translation, for example, ‘to show … actually …’

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Accept As True
s.d: to accept, but with the implication of the truth being difficult to comprehend or to respond to properly

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Patience, Endurance, Perseverance
s.d: to put up with annoyance or difficulty
s.g: to put up with; to endure

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Ripen, Produce Fruit, Bear Seed
s.d: to produce fruit or seed (of plants)
s.g: to bear fruit; to produce fruit; to produce seed; to yield

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Ripen, Produce Fruit, Bear Seed
s.d: to produce fruit or seed (of plants)
s.g: to bear fruit; to produce fruit; to produce seed; to yield

s.dp: Linear Movement › Move, Come/Go
s.d: to move from one place to another, with the possible implication of causing the movement of some other object or objects
s.g: to move; to come; to blow
s.c: It is possible that in ⟦Acts 2:2|Acts 2:2⟧ φέρομαι should be understood in an idiomatic sense of ‘blowing,’ since it is combined with the noun for ‘wind’ (πνοή, LN 14.4). In any event, one must often translate φέρομαι as ‘blowing,’ since this is frequently the appropriate type of term to use in speaking of the movement of wind.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of φέρομαι[a] ‘to move from one place to another,’ {D:15.11}) to change from one state to another, with the implication of progressive development
s.g: to change to; to move on to; to progress

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move quickly from a point or area in order to avoid presumed danger or difficulty
s.g: to run away; to flee; flight

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Become Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: to become safe from danger by avoiding or escaping{N:001}

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Exist
s.d: to cease rapidly to exist
s.g: to cease quickly; to disappear rapidly
s.c: For another interpretation of φεύγω in ⟦Revelation 16:20|Revelation 16:20⟧, see LN 24.6.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:φεύγω<SDBG:φεύγω:000000>}[a] ‘to flee,’ {D:15.61}) to avoid doing something, with the evident purpose of attempting to avoid danger

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:φεύγω<SDBG:φεύγω:000000>}[a] ‘to flee,’ {D:15.61}) to disappear quickly from sight
s.c: For another interpretation of φεύγω in ⟦Revelation 16:20|Revelation 16:20⟧, see LN 13.95.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a procurator of Palestine

s.dp: Communication › Inform, Announce
s.d: information concerning a person or an event

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: to speak or talk, with apparent focus upon the content of what is said
s.g: to say; to talk; to tell; to speak

s.dp: Communication › Interpret, Mean, Explain
s.d: to say something in order to explain more fully the implications or intent of what has been said

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: Porcius Festus, the successor to Felix as procurator of Palestine; see {D:93.300}

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to move toward and to arrive at a point{N:001}
s.g: to come to; to reach; to arrive

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go Prior To
s.d: to come/go prior to some other event, normally one involving a similar type of movement
s.g: to come/go prior to; to come/go beforehand; to precede
s.c: Though the movement referred to by φθάνω and προέρχομαι may involve movement which is spacially ahead of someone else, nevertheless the focus of meaning is not a spacial relationship but a temporal one.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to attain or arrive at a particular state{N:002}
s.g: to come to be; to attain; to achieve
s.c: Though grammatically it is the law which is not attained in ⟦Romans 9:31|Romans 9:31⟧, semantically it is, of course, the state of righteousness which was the ultimate goal, and hence it was this particular state which was not attained.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to happen to someone prior to a particular point in time
s.g: to happen to already; to come upon; to come upon already

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: pertaining to that which is bound to disintegrate and die

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: to speak, with focus upon verbal sound rather than upon content

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Destroy
s.d: to ruin or destroy something, with the implication of causing something to be corrupt and thus to cease to exist

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Harm, Wound
s.d: to cause harm to someone
s.c: It may be possible to translate this expression in ⟦2 Corinthians 7:2|2 Corinthians 7:2⟧ (referring to financial ruin) as ‘we have not caused anyone to suffer a loss,’ but φθείρω in ⟦2 Corinthians 7:2|2 Corinthians 7:2⟧ may also refer to the undermining of faith.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Licentiousness, Perversion
s.d: to cause someone to become perverse or depraved, as a type of moral destruction{N:001}
s.g: to deprave; to pervert; to ruin; to cause the moral ruin of

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: pertaining to the latter part of autumn
s.c: The use of φθινοπωρινός in ⟦Jude 1:12|Jude 1:12⟧ should not be understood to imply that the fruit has already been picked, but rather that the trees in question have not produced fruit at all, and even in late autumn there is no productivity.

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Sound
s.d: any type of sound, including human speech, but normally a distinctive type of sound as opposed to confused noise
s.c: In many languages an important distinction is made between verbal sounds, that is to say, the sounds of speech, and non-verbal sounds. In some languages musical sounds also require a very special type of terminology, often with distinctions made depending upon the type of instrument involved.

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: (derivative of {L:φθέγγομαι<SDBG:φθέγγομαι:000000>} ‘to utter,’ {D:33.76}) an utterance, with possible focus upon the clarity of the verbal sounds

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Envy, Jealousy
s.d: to experience a feeling of ill will due to real or presumed advantage experienced by someone else
s.g: to be envious; to be jealous

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Envy, Jealousy
s.d: a state of ill will toward someone because of some real or presumed advantage experienced by such a person
s.c: Expressions for ‘envy’ or ‘jealousy’ are often idiomatic, for example, ‘the heart burns’ or ‘the stomach is hot.’

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Destroy
s.d: a state of ruin or destruction, with the implication of disintegration
s.c: In ⟦2 Peter 2:12|2 Peter 2:12⟧ it may be more appropriate in a number of languages to translate ‘… to be killed.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Rot, Decay
s.d: to rot or decay, in reference to organic matter

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Licentiousness, Perversion
s.d: a state of moral corruption and depravity
s.c: In some languages ‘slaves of moral corruption’ in ⟦2 Peter 2:19|2 Peter 2:19⟧ may be expressed as ‘their immoral desires make slaves of them’ or ‘… cause them to be slaves.’

s.dp: Artifacts › Containers
s.d: a broad, shallow bowl, normally used for cooking or for serving liquids

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: pertaining to liking or loving what is good
s.g: liking what is good; loving what is good

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city in the west central part of Asia Minor

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: affection for one’s fellow believer in Christ
s.g: love for one’s fellow believer; affection for a fellow believer
s.c: In the NT the terms φιλαδελφία and φιλάδελφος (LN 25.35) have acquired highly specialized meanings which restrict the range of reference to fellow believers. In nonbiblical contexts these terms would refer to affection or love for persons belonging to a so-called ‘in-group,’ but in the NT this in-group is defined in terms of Christian faith.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: pertaining to love or affection for fellow believers
s.g: one who loves fellow believers; loving one another as brothers
s.c: See discussion at LN 25.34.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: pertaining to having affection for a husband
s.g: having love for one’s husband; having affection for one’s husband

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: affection for people in general
s.g: love of mankind; affection for people

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Kindness, Harshness
s.d: to show friendly concern for someone

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Kindness, Harshness
s.d: pertaining to friendly concern and kindness toward someone

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: the state of loving money or wealth
s.g: love of wealth; love of money

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: pertaining to the love of wealth or money

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: pertaining to self-centered love or concern for one’s own self

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: to have love or affection for someone or something based on association
s.g: to love; to have affection for
s.c: See the discussion of the meaning of φιλέω and φιλία in LN 25.43.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: to particularly like or enjoy doing something
s.g: to like to; to love to

s.dp: Association › Kiss, Embrace
s.d: to kiss, either as an expression of greeting or as a sign of special affection and appreciation{N:001}
s.c: Since in so many societies kissing is not a form of greeting, it may be necessary to add some kind of classifier to contexts such as ⟦Matthew 26:48|Matthew 26:48⟧ and ⟦Matthew 26:49|Matthew 26:49⟧ in order to indicate clearly the intention involved; otherwise, the use of a term meaning merely ‘to kiss’ might suggest a kind of erotic display. The clause in ⟦Matthew 26:49|Matthew 26:49⟧ may be translated as ‘the man I greet by kissing is the one you want.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: pertaining to being fond of pleasure and enjoyment
s.g: given over to pleasure; lover of pleasure; loving pleasure

s.dp: Association › Kiss, Embrace
s.d: to kiss, either as an expression of greeting or as a sign of special affection and appreciation

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a convert and friend of Paul

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a false teacher in the church

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: to have love or affection for someone or something based on association
s.g: to love; to have affection for
s.c: In a number of languages it may be difficult if not impossible to speak of ‘affection … is hostility.’ Frequently it is necessary to relate such emotional attitudes to individuals, so that this expression in ⟦James 4:4|James 4:4⟧ may be rendered in some languages as ‘people who love the things in the world are against God.’|See the discussion of the meaning of φιλέω and φιλία in LN 25.43.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Φίλιπποι<SDBG:Φίλιπποι:000000>} ‘Philippi,’ {D:93.605}) a person who lives in or is a native of Philippi

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city in Macedonia
s.c: For Καισάρεια τῆς Φιλίππου 'Caesarea Philippi,' see LN 93.492

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: one of the twelve apostles

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a son of Herod the Great and brother of Herod Antipas

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: one of the seven helpers in the church in Jerusalem

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the first husband of Herodias

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: Caesarea Philippi at the foot of Mount Hermon; see also {D:93.605}

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: pertaining to love for God
s.g: loving God; having affection for God

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person greeted in {S:04501601500004}

s.dp: Communication › Argue, Quarrel
s.d: readiness or desire to argue or quarrel
s.g: desire to quarrel; readiness to argue; to want to argue; quarrelsomeness

s.dp: Communication › Argue, Quarrel
s.d: pertaining to being desirous of arguing

s.dp: Association › Show Hospitality
s.d: receiving and showing hospitality to a stranger, that is, someone who is not regarded as a member of the extended family or a close friend
s.g: hospitality; receiving a stranger as a guest
s.c: To receive a stranger as a guest is sometimes expressed idiomatically as ‘to let a stranger sit at one’s table,’ ‘to offer a bed to a stranger,’ or ‘to let a stranger enter one’s house.’

s.dp: Association › Show Hospitality
s.d: pertaining to showing hospitality to strangers

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
s.d: to like or love to be first in rank or position
s.g: to desire to be first; to desire to order others

s.dp: Association › Associate
s.d: a male person with whom one associates and for whom there is affection or personal regard
s.c: In some languages there are different terms for different grades of friends, that is to say, a difference between intimate friends with whom one constantly shares and those who constitute a somewhat wider circle of persons who are on friendly terms but who are not in the inner circle of intimate relations. The choice of terms for ‘friend’ will depend, of course, upon individual contexts.

s.dp: Association › Associate
s.d: a female person with whom one associates and for whom there is affection or personal regard
s.c: See discussion at LN 34.11.

s.dp: Understand › Capacity for Understanding
s.d: human understanding or wisdom and, by implication, in contrast with divinely revealed knowledge
s.c: In ⟦Colossians 2:8|Colossians 2:8⟧ φιλοσοφία may be rendered in some languages as ‘the way in which people are wise’ or ‘the way in which people understand things’ or ‘the manner in which people reason.’

s.dp: Understand › Capacity for Understanding
s.d: a person of professional or semi-professional status regarded as having particular capacity or competence in understanding the meaning or significance of human experience
s.c: In some instances φιλόσοφος in ⟦Acts 17:18|Acts 17:18⟧ may be translated simply as ‘teacher,’ since such a word would normally designate a professional or semi-professional person involved in scholarly activities.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: pertaining to love or affection for those closely related to one, particularly members of one’s immediate family or in-group
s.g: very loving; warmly devoted to; very affectionate

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Love, Affection, Compassion
s.d: pertaining to having affection for one’s own offspring
s.g: loving one’s own children; one who loves children

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
s.d: to earnestly aspire to something, implying strong ambition for some goal
s.g: to aspire to; to make something one’s ambition to
s.c: An equivalent of φιλοτιμεῖσθαι ἡσυχάζειν in ⟦1 Thessalonians 4:11|1 Thessalonians 4:11⟧ may be in some languages ‘do everything you can to live the quiet life.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Kindness, Harshness
s.d: pertaining to friendly concern and kindness toward someone

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person greeted in {S:04501601400006}

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Burning
s.d: to cause the process of burning to begin
s.g: to ignite; to kindle; to set ablaze; to start a fire; to light a lamp
s.c: As already noted in the series of terms listed in LN 14.63, languages differ appreciably in terms employed for different phases and results of burning. For example, to set something on fire for the sake of providing warmth may be expressed by quite a different term from that which is used in speaking of the process of setting something on fire in order to destroy it.

s.dp: Natural Substances › Fire
s.d: the burning vapor surrounding an object on fire
s.c: As in the case of πῦρa ‘fire’ (LN 2.3), the term φλόξ ‘flame’ is likewise frequently rendered by a verb rather than by a noun. Accordingly, in a passage such as ⟦Acts 7:30|Acts 7:30⟧ ‘in the flames of a burning bush’ becomes ‘where the burning bush was flaming up’ or ‘where flames were burning a bush.’ In some languages ‘flames’ are referred to as ‘the tongues of the fire’ or ‘the banner of the fire.’ In a number of languages, however, no distinction is made between ‘fire’ and ‘flame.’

s.dp: Communication › Foolish Talk
s.d: to speak in such a way as to make no sense, presumably because of ignorance of what is involved
s.c: In some languages ‘to talk nonsense’ is ‘to talk without understanding what one is saying,’ but in other instances an equivalent may be ‘to talk without anybody being able to understand what one is saying.’

s.dp: Communication › Foolish Talk
s.d: (derivative of {L:φλυαρέω<SDBG:φλυαρέω:000000>} ‘to talk nonsense,’ {D:33.374}) pertaining to talking nonsense
s.c: It is possible that in ⟦1 Timothy 5:13|1 Timothy 5:13⟧ φλύαρος should be rendered as ‘gossipy’ in view of the fact that one who speaks nonsense about someone else is normally gossiping.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Fear, Terror, Alarm
s.d: pertaining to something or someone who causes fear

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Fear, Terror, Alarm
s.d: (derivative of {L:φόβος<SDBG:φόβος:000000>}[a] ‘fear,’ {D:25.251}) to be in a state of fearing

s.dp: Status › Honor or Respect in Relation to Status
s.d: to have such awe or respect for a person as to involve a measure of fear
s.g: to fear; to show great reverence for; to show great respect for
s.c: In a number of languages there are serious problems involved in speaking of ‘fearing God,’ for this might imply merely ‘to be scared of God’ as though God were some kind of bogeyman. If there is a term with the meaning of ‘awe’ (perhaps in a phrase such as ‘to stand in awe of’), this may be an adequate equivalent. In some instances awe is expressed idiomatically as ‘to stand with one’s heart in one’s throat’ or ‘to be in someone’s presence with one’s heart beating fast.’

s.dp: Religious Activities › Worship, Reverence
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:φοβέω<SDBG:φοβέω:000000>}[a] ‘to fear,’ {D:25.252}) to have profound reverence and respect for deity, with the implication of awe bordering on fear
s.c: In ⟦Acts 13:16|Acts 13:16⟧ the phrase οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν θεόν, literally ‘those who fear God,’ is essentially a technical phrase to identify non-Jews who worshiped the God of the Jews. These would have been Gentiles who were ‘God fearers’ or ‘worshipers of God.’
